title: feat(ask): an affinity key that keeps asks with a shared prefix on one endpoint and replica
description:
## .what

an openrouter ask has no way to tie a set of asks that share a prompt prefix to one served endpoint or one replica, so a prompt cache written by one ask is rarely read by the next.

checkable evidence: genBrainAtom.js (0.1.3) sends model, messages, and response_format, and no session or affinity header; the string affinity appears nowhere in its dist. in ehmpathy/rhachet-roles-bhrain:
- two review lanes with byte-identical 152,119-byte heads, fired 62ms apart, read cache.get 0 on both (340,382 and 489,260 input tokens)
- one static head read 1,408 cached at 17:28 and 0 at 18:06, 90s after a peer lane sent it
- on one host (coreweave), 8 of 9 asks read their identical prefix warm at 99.7% and one read 0%: same host, different replica
- with a prime ask before a pour of N asks in place on the consumer side, each lane still read at most a sliver (0 of 306,318; 1,280 of 587,937)

## .why

a consumer that splits one large review into N asks over a ~200k shared prefix primes the prefix once, then pours the N. without a pin, throttled asks fall to suppliers that never saw the prefix and pay it at full rate. the fireworks adapter already solves the replica half with an x-session-affinity key derived from the system prompt; the openrouter path has no equivalent.

## .shape of the fix

    await brainAtom.ask({ role, prompt, schema, affinity: { key } }, context);

1. the first ask with a key records the endpoint that served it (on disk, short ttl such as 10 min)
2. later asks with the same key try that endpoint first, still inside every filter (floor, privacy, speed); fall back only on refusal or throttle, and say so in supply.attempts
3. where the supplier supports replica affinity, forward the key as a session / affinity hint
4. supply reports affinity { key, hit }, so a caller can measure whether the pin held
5. default: derive the key from the system prompt when the caller gives none, as the fireworks adapter does

acceptance: N asks with one key and no throttle report one supply.provider; a refusal on the pinned endpoint falls back and reports a miss; an ask with no key and no system prompt behaves exactly as today.

related: #16 (rank endpoints by expected billed cost with cache) picks a host that caches; this keeps a prefix set on it.
